Subject: Short-cycle renewal: opt-in bridge credit and invoice split

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation about aligning your renewal to Luminosys' fiscal cadence, I wanted to propose a short-cycle renewal option that helps you avoid a mid-year budget cliff while keeping unit economics predictable. High-level offer: 

- Term: 9 months (starts on signature) to co-term with your existing enterprise agreement on 2027-03-31.
- Uplift: 8% on current committed capacity to account for mid-contract provisioning.
- Opt-in bridge credit: If Luminosys signs and submits PO within 30 days, we will apply a one-time 10% credit (voucher) against the first invoice. Credit applies only to committed capacity and cannot be combined with other promotional discounts.
- Invoice split: We can split the first charge across two invoices to match your Q3/Q4 spend windows (we usually do 60/40 or custom).

Attached: a draft amendment and an invoice schedule template so your procurement team has something tangible to review.

Ask: can you confirm whether procurement needs a full contract redline + SOW or if the amendment + PO will be sufficient? Also, do you prefer a 60/40 split for the first invoice or something else?

If this looks good I’ll loop in Ben on the formal quote and DocuSign flow.

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Appreciate the clear proposal. A couple quick notes from my side and I’ve looped in Procurement so they can confirm PO timing.

- The 10% bridge credit is compelling — can you confirm whether that is refundable if we exceed committed capacity in the first 60 days? Our finance team likes clarity on credits vs. rebates.

Looping you both in. Alex asked about whether the 10% bridge credit is refundable if they overshoot committed capacity in the first 60 days. My recommendation below: make the credit conditional (non-refundable) but applicable only to committed capacity; any overage will be billed at standard overage rates and will not reduce the credit. - Offer a capped overage protection for the first 30 days (e.g., first 10k tokens of overage billed at 50% list) as a one-time concession to ease adoption.
- Provide a clean amendment (no redline needed for start) plus a redline version if Procurement insists.
